---
title: "Install soundscapy"
guide-section: "How-to"
---

This page installs soundscapy into a new project folder and checks that it works. You
need only a terminal; the scripts install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), which
provides Python for you.

## On your own computer

### Step 1: save the first-plot code

Make an empty folder for your project and save this code in it as `_quickstart.py`:

{{< include _quickstart.py >}}

### Step 2: save the install script

Save the script for your system in the same folder, as `_quickstart.ps1` on Windows or
`_quickstart.sh` on macOS and Linux. It installs uv if it is missing, creates a project in
the folder, adds soundscapy and JupyterLab to it, and runs `_quickstart.py`.

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Windows (PowerShell)

{{< include _quickstart.ps1 lang="powershell" >}}

#### macOS and Linux

{{< include _quickstart.sh >}}

:::

### Step 3: run it

Open a terminal in the folder and run the script. On Windows, the `Bypass` flag lets a
saved script run under PowerShell's default execution policy.

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Windows (PowerShell)

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File _quickstart.ps1
```

#### macOS and Linux

```bash
sh _quickstart.sh
```

:::

It prints the installed soundscapy version. Running it again in the same folder is safe.

The pin `soundscapy==1.0.0.dev1` names a pre-release exactly, so uv installs it without
needing `--prerelease`.

Then open JupyterLab in the project and paste the same code into a notebook cell:

```bash
uv run jupyter lab
```

## Hosted notebook

In a hosted notebook such as Google Colab, install soundscapy with one cell:

```python
%pip install 'soundscapy==1.0.0.dev1'
```

Then run the same code in the next cell:

{{< include _quickstart.py >}}
